# Set up

Load needed packages, make sure they are installed.

```{r}
library(readr) 
library(dplyr) 
library(tidyverse) 
library(skimr) 
library(here)
library(tibble)
```

Load the data.

```{r}
#Path to data dictionary. Note the use of the here() package and not absolute paths
data_location <- here("Data","raw-data","TB_data_dictionary_2026-09-25.csv")
#load data dictionary
data_dictionary <- read_csv(data_location)

#Path to dataframes. 
data_location1 <- here("Data", "raw-data", "TB_burden_countries_2026-09-29.csv")
burden_data <- read_csv(data_location1)

data_location2 <- here("Data", "raw-data", "LTBI_estimates_2026-09-29.csv")
household_data <- read_csv(data_location2)

data_location3 <- here("Data", "raw-data", "TB_hiv_nonroutine_surveillance_2026-09-29.csv")
hiv_surveillance_data <- read_csv(data_location3)

data_location4 <- here("Data", "raw-data", "TB_contact_tpt_2026-09-29.csv")
contact_screening_data <- read_csv(data_location4)

data_location5 <- here("Data", "raw-data", "TB_policies_services_2026-09-29.csv")
policies_data <- read_csv(data_location5)

```

Use dictionary to make dataframes more readable

```{r}
##Full joining

join1 <- full_join(burden_data, contact_screening_data, by = c("country", "year"))

join2 <- full_join(hiv_surveillance_data, join1, by = c("country", "year"))

join3 <- full_join(household_data, join2, by = c("country", "year"))

full_join_data <- full_join(policies_data, join3, by = c("country", "year"))

```
